HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE JAVED IQBAL WANI, JUDGE  JUDGEMENT 1.

The petitioners in the instant petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India have prayed for the following reliefs:
i) Writ of mandamus directing the respondent No. 4 i.e., Collector, Land Acquisition/SDM Awantipora to work out the compensation payable to the petitioners for their aforesaid acquired land in terms of the aforesaid provisions of Ghulam Rasool Wani (Aged 68 Years) vs Union Territory Of J&K on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77900664/
1 "The Jammu and Kashmir Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013" at the prevalent market fixed for the year 2022 under the Stamp Act.

sentences.text:
ii. Writ of mandamus directing the respondent no. 4 i.e., Collector Land Acquisition/SDM Awantipora to work outthe solatium and statutory interest as may be payable to the petitioners in terms of "the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
iii. Writ of mandamus directing the respondents to pay the aforesaid compensation, solatium and statutory interest payable to the petitioners as may be worked out by the respondent no.4 i.e.,
Collector Land Acquisition/SDM Awantipora after the necessary deduction of the payment of compensation already received by them in lieu of their aforesaid acquired land."
2.

The facts giving rise to the filing of the instant petition as stated in the petition are that the petitioner 1 owned and possessed land measuring 4 kanals, 122 square feet under khasra no. 1639, 1 kanal 6 sirsai under khasra no. 1638, and petitioner 2 owned and possessed 2 kanals, 19 marlas 150 sft under khasra no. 1639 situated at Pampore on the main old Srinagar-Jammu Highway.

The said land along with some other land of the adjacent land owners came to be requisitioned for acquisition by respondent 6 herein for public purpose being establishment of "Bulk LPG Tank cum Truck Parking for the LPG Bottling Plant Pampore" and an intent in this regard came to be placed by respondent 6 before respondent 5 herein on 26.07.2017 whereupon a notification under section 4 of J&K Land Acquisition Act, Samvat 1990 (for short "the Act of 1990") came to be issued on 17.11.2017 followed by private negotiations held on 5.3.2019 between the parties under the chairmanship of respondent 3 herein and Rs.40/- lacs per kanal came to be fixed as rate of land per kanaland consequently apportionment of compensation payable to the petitioners herein and other land owners came to be made, however, the said compensation was not paid to the petitioners for more than 2  years compelling the petitioners to approach respondent 2 herein with a plea that the private negotiations held earlier had lost validity and the then rates fixed for the land are not acceptable to them and that a legal notice as well came to be served upon the respondents by the petitioners inter alia through their counsel on 25.01.2021 in this regard wherein the petitioners claimed compensation for the land in question under "The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013"
(hereinafter referred to as "the Act of 2013") along with statutory interest, but the respondents finally chose to make the payment of compensation to the petitioners along with other land owners according to the terms of the private negotiations held on 05.03.2019 which amount of compensation came to be received by the petitioners under protest.
3.

The petitioners thus while maintaining the instant petition and seeking the aforesaid reliefs have insisted that the fixed for the land in question during private negotiations held on 05.03.2019 have ceased it be operative on account of delayed payment of compensation made to the petitioners on Ghulam Rasool Wani (Aged 68 Years) vs Union Territory Of J&K on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77900664/

sentences.text: one hand and on the other are contending to be entitled to compensation of the land in question under the Act of 2013 in view of coming into being operational of the said Act.

4. Objections to the petition have been filed by the respondents wherein the petition is being opposed, inter alia, on the grounds that the petitioners are not entitled to the reliefs as are prayed in the petition while admitting that the land in question of the petitioners came to be acquired under private negotiations held by the Private Negotiations Committee with the officers of the intending department, the petitioners and the members of the Revenue department under the chairmanship of the Deputy Commissioner, Pulwama, which negotiations finally got completed on 05.03.2019 deciding the rate of the land at Rs. 40/- lacs per kanal along with 1% administrative charges and that the total compensation amounting to Rs.7.05 crores came to be assessed out of which Rs.3/- crores were deposited in the District Treasury Pulwama on 25.10.2017 followed by depositing of the remaining Rs.4.10 crores on 1.8.2019 including charges of the planted trees existing on the subject land.
It is stated by respondent 6 in the objections that the plea of the application of the Act of 2013 raised by the petitioners stands addressed by the official respondents and found not applicable to the case of the petitioners in view of Clause 13 of J&K Reorganisation Order No. 2019 wherein under Sub Clause (14) it is provided that proceedings already initiated under the Land Acquisition Act 1990,
(for short Repealed Act) shall be continued and be completed as per the procedure provided under the said Act.

It is further stated in the objections that after successfully completing the private negotiations the Deputy Commissioner Pulwama provided final award letter on 26.03.2019 and that the award amount stands deposited within the prescribed period before the concerned authority and thus the petitioners cannot maintain the instant petition.

In the objections filed by the respondents 1 to 5 to the petition, it is being admitted that the land acquisition proceedings were undertaken at the request of intending department by issuance of a notification under section 4 on 17.11.2017 in respect of land measuring 17 kanals 9 marlas including the subject land whereafter private negotiations came to be undertaken on 05.03.2019 and Rs.40/-lacs came to be fixed as the rate per kanal of land in consensus with the persons involved in the said proceedings whereupon total apportionment was assessed at Rs. 7,04,98,000/- including 1 per cent administrative charges and an amount of Rs. 5,41,917/- came to be assessed in respect of fruit/non-fruit bearing trees standing thereon and that since the amount likely to be paid was found beyond the pecuniary jurisdiction of the Collector, necessary approval, as such, became imperative from the higher authorities and after inter se correspondences made in this regard as also for clarifying certain issues and observations made, approval came to be accorded by the competent authority/Financial Commissioner on 10.04.2022 whereupon the payments came to be made in favour of the persons interested through their respective bank accounts.
It is further stated in the objections that the amount of compensation stands received by the petitioners as had been agreed by them in the private negotiation meeting held on 05.03.2019 and that the dissatisfaction shown by the petitioner about the amount of compensation received by them is an afterthought though the appropriate legal course of reference can be invoked by the petitioners instead of seeking recourse to the provisions of Act of 2013.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties, perused the record and considered the matter.

5. The core issue which arises for consideration of this court having regard to the case set up by the parties in their respective pleadings is as to whether the instant petition is maintainable and the reliefs as prayed for by the petitioners are capable of being granted to the petitioners by this court.

6. It is an admitted fact emerging from the record that the subject land came to be requisitioned for acquisition by the respondents 6 herein through respondent 5 herein and in furtherance thereof respondent 5 issued a notification under section 4 of the Act of 1990 on 17.11.2017.

It is also not in dispute that the process of acquisition of the subject of land was proceeded under private negotiations conducted by the District Private Negotiations Committee consisting of the officers of the intending Department, the members of the Revenue Department as also the petitioners herein along with other landowners under the chairmanship of Deputy Commissioner, Pulwama respondent 3 herein.

7. Record available on the file inasmuch as that produced by the counsel for the official respondents bears testimony to the fact that in the said private negotiations the rate of subject land came to be fixed at Rs. 40/- lacs per kanal, which was accepted and acknowledged by all the members of the District Private Negotiations Committee including the petitioners herein.

The record further indisputably tends to show that the amount of compensation assessed of the subject of land came to be paid to the petitioners somewhere in the month of April 2021 having been accepted by the petitioners under protest.

The plea of the respondents 1 to 5 raised in the objections that the payment of the said compensation to the petitioners got delayed on account of the various queries raised in the matter including on account of the lack of pecuniary jurisdiction of the District Collector has neither been disputed nor denied by the petitioners in the rejoinder affidavit filed to the reply filed by the respondents 1 to 5 to the petition, so also has not been denied the plea of the saving of the acquisition proceedings undertaken under the Act of 1990 after coming into being of Reorganization Act of 2019.
8. Having regard to the aforesaid facts, circumstances and the position obtaining in the matter

,
indisputably there has been an agreement between the parties in the Private Negotiations as regards the value of the subject land having resulted into the passing of the consent award.

Under these circumstances the petitioners cannot join an issue now qua the said agreement that too in the instant petition or else maintain the same for seeking the aforesaid reliefs as the petitioners, in law will be precluded and estopped thereof.

A reference in this regard to the judgement of the Apex Court passed in case titled as 'State of State of Karnataka and another v. Sangappa Dyavappa Biradar and others' reported in (2005) 4 SCC 264 wherein at Paragraph 12 following has been held:
". . .

entities.text: State of State of Karnataka and another v. Sangappa Dyavappa Biradar and others' reported in (2005) 4 SCC 264
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A right of a landholder to obtain an order of reference would arise only when he has not accepted the award.
Once such award is accepted, no legal right in him survives for claiming a reference to the Civil Court.
An agreement between the parties as regard the value of the lands acquired by the State is binding on the parties.

So long as such agreement and consequently the consent awards are not set aside in an appropriate proceeding by a court of law having jurisdiction in relation thereto, the Ghulam Rasool Wani (Aged 68 Years) vs Union Territory Of J&K on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77900664/
4 same remain binding.

entities.text: Ghulam Rasool Wani (Aged 68 Years) vs Union Territory Of J&K
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is one thing to say that agreements are void or voidable in terms of the provisions of the Indian Contract Act having been obtained by fraud,
collusion, etc, or are against public policy but it is another thing to say that without questioning the validity thereof, the Respondents could have maintained their writ petitions."
9.
Viewed thus what has been observed, considered and analysed hereinabove, the instant petition is held to be not maintainable inasmuch as lacing merit.

Accordingly, the petition is dismissed,
however, without any costs.
10. The record produced by the counsel for the respondents is directed to be returned back.
